steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Covalent bond: A shared pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms. Each atom contributes one electron to the shared pair. Both atoms achieve a full outer shell. | Simple molecular substance: A substance made up of separate molecules, each containing a fixed number of atoms joined by covalent bonds (e.g. H₂O, CO₂). | Giant covalent structure: A huge network of atoms all joined by covalent bonds in a giant lattice (e.g. diamond, graphite). | Intermolecular forces: Weak forces of attraction between molecules (NOT between atoms within a molecule). These are much weaker than covalent bonds.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Foundation Describe how a covalent bond forms.
